speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to begin our assessment, how long has this symptom been present, and has it been constant or intermittent?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: The mechanism of injury—a jersey pulled forcefully off your ring finger two days ago—suggests a significant strain or ligament injury. Can you point to the exact location of the maximum tenderness, and do you have any numbness or tingling in that finger?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Extensor Tendon Avulsion). The history of a pulling force combined with your inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint, pain at that specific joint, and the finger resting in extension is classic for this injury. Please submit an X-RAY of the right hand to check for an avulsion fracture and confirm the diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
